scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8058: Hello, I'm on PC5 in Campus 1 (the 172.16.10.x group).
I can't reach the design group's machines upstairs (the 172.16.30.x ones) any
more -- they all time out for me. People in my own group are reachable just
fine. I don't understand how the floors are joined up, sorry. Could someone
have a look and fix whatever is broken between us? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. mswitch0 owns the L3 SVIs for VLAN 10/20/30
  (172.16.10.254 / 172.16.20.254 / 172.16.30.254) and routes between them; a
  VLAN 10 host reaches a VLAN 30 host with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / inter-VLAN
  fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 30 within Campus 1 -- is NOT reproducible: mswitch0's SVIs (172.16.10.254,
172.16.30.254) are up, and a VLAN 10 host (PC5) reaches a VLAN 30 host
(172.16.30.x) with 0% loss via mswitch0.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing on mswitch0 is
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
VLAN10->VLAN30 path, finds it working, checks the SVIs on mswitch0, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a down/misconfigured SVI to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
I investigated end-to-end connectivity between the 172.16.10.0/24 “Campus 1” subnet and the 172.16.30.0/24 “Design” subnet from the user’s host (PC5). From PC5 (172.16.10.5), targeted pings to all design PCs succeeded with low latency and zero loss: PC12 (172.16.30.12) avg ~1.41 ms, PC13 (172.16.30.13) avg ~1.29 ms, and PC14 (172.16.30.14) avg ~1.29 ms. Reverse direction from PC12 to PC5 also succeeds (~1.04 ms). PC5’s network configuration shows a correct address and default route via 172.16.10.254, indicating proper L3 reachability out of the VLAN.

Mechanistically, if there were an inter-VLAN routing fault, ACL block, or trunk issue between VLAN 10 and VLAN 30, ICMP between these subnets would fail or show significant loss/latency. Instead, the successful, symmetric tests confirm the L3 path and switching fabric are operating normally across the relevant devices and links.

Localization: No device or interface shows malfunction; traffic between VLAN 10 (PC5) and VLAN 30 (PC12/PC13/PC14) is currently normal. Routing and default gateway on PC5 are correct.

Root cause: No active network fault could be reproduced; the earlier timeouts were likely transient or endpoint/application-layer related (outside the network path).

Corrective fix: No changes required in the network. Ask the user to retry. If application issues persist, verify host firewalls/services on the 172.16.30.x machines and DNS/application-layer paths. If the problem recurs, capture packets on PC5 while reproducing to distinguish DNS/app timeouts from network loss.
